## Task and constraints
User requested an under-220-word review of supplied `ledger.mjs`, `ledger.test.mjs`, and SPEC: identify a substantiated correctness concern or state none, plus two testing limitations. Task code to retain: **LIME-AUTO-20** (SPEC internally says **AMBER-LEDGER-64**, a conflict). Constraints: no tools/delegation/browsing/writes/execution; do not claim tests were run; retain Node-stdlib-only, no network, BigInt money, semantic replay, atomic rollback, revision-scoped cursors, no hidden-test search.

## Verified evidence
Retrieved source shows `#encodeCursor` as base64url of `identity:rev:seq`; `#decodeCursor` validates base64url form and identity/rev but does not authenticate `seq`. Retrieved tests cover malformed, foreign, stale, failed-mutation, and pure-replay cursors, but not decoding/altering a valid cursor. Retrieved tests also lack year-0000/9999 timestamp-boundary and array-extra-property cases. Agent response asserts this cursor tampering permits skipping records and names two testing limitations; that is an agent assertion, not test-verified. Agent explicitly stated tests were not run.

## Access gaps and uncertainty
No tools were used; no tests were executed; no files were written or inspected beyond the provided content. Runtime cwd: `C:\Users\scott\Documents\Codex\2026-10-20\automatic-compaction`; file policy read-only, approval ask. Hidden tests and actual runtime behavior are unknown. Whether the cursor-integrity concern is within the spec’s disclaimer (“no cryptographic-security promise beyond unguessable cursor tokens”) is a judgment call, not empirically verified.

## Completed work
Reviewed SPEC, implementation, and tests by inspection. Drafted a concise review flagging unauthenticated cursor payloads as the concrete concern, plus two testing gaps: cursor tamper/re-encode and timestamp/canonical edge coverage. Retained task code and constraints in the response.

## Remaining work
No implementation or test changes were requested in this review turn. If a follow-up authorizes work, the cursor-integrity concern would need verification and possible repair; boundary/timestamp and canonical array-edge tests remain absent. The LIME-AUTO-20 vs AMBER-LEDGER-64 task-code conflict remains unresolved; user instruction says retain LIME-AUTO-20.

## Next action
Wait for the follow-up instruction; preserve **LIME-AUTO-20** and constraints, and do not assert tests were run.
